title: Ning Li's gravito-magnetic research moves to Redstone Arsenal
place_text: University of Alabama-Huntsville / Redstone Arsenal, Alabama

tellings.quote: Li was a woman who eventually left her position at the University of Alabama-Huntsville to [music] work full-time at Redstone Arsenal on research so sensitive, it effectively vanished from public view.
Her story took an even darker turn in 2014 when she was struck by a car on the University of Alabama campus and suffered permanent brain [music] damage.
tellings.difference: Adds that she was hit by a car on the University of Alabama campus in 2014 and suffered permanent brain damage, and runs the timeline up to 2021.
tellings.link_reason: Same story: Ning Li's gravity research moves into classified work and disappears from public view.

as_told.title: Ning Li's gravity research vanishes into classified world

plain: In the 1990s, the physicist Ning Li is said to have left her job at the University of Alabama in Huntsville to work full-time at Redstone Arsenal, a US Army base in Alabama, on research into gravity and magnetism so sensitive that it effectively vanished from public view. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and mentions her colleagues Larry Smalley and Douglas Torr. In a second episode he adds that in 2014 she was hit by a car on the University of Alabama campus and was left with permanent brain damage, and he follows her story up to 2021.
